style.vernacular: Hot-humid tropical city of painted-concrete and brick low- and mid-rise buildings: two- to four-storey Chinese shophouses with five-foot-way arcades in cream, pastel and faded ochre; terracotta- or grey-tile pitched roofs on Malay-influenced civic buildings and mosques; modernist 1960s-70s concrete blocks with sunbreakers; sprawling malls and glass towers; mosques with a large central dome and a tall slender minaret. Heavy rain-tree, palm and angsana planting, monsoon drains and elevated rail.
style.ornament: Islamic geometric lattice screens and arches on mosques and civic buildings; Minangkabau-style up-curved roof gables on some government and Malay-heritage buildings; Mughal-Moorish arches, copper domes and clock tower on colonial civic buildings; five-foot-way arcades, louvred shutters and ceramic tile dado on shophouses; precast sunbreakers on 1960s modernist blocks.

sources.what: Malaysian architecture overview: timber Malay houses on stilts, colonial Mughal/Tudor/Gothic Revival, KLIA wood-strip roof
modernist concrete parliament with terrazzo sunbreakers and heat-absorbing glass on a 17-storey tower
